application_review: PROGRESS. Previous audit rechecked and all baseline proof hashes preserved.
Subtraction of finite Haar means is exact. The comparison lemma requires a nonempty finite type before using the absolute mean bound.
The short-cube theorem assumes positive floor(q/(J*a)), establishing nonempty increment types before both averaging steps. The root mean is reordered by an already proved finite triple-mean identity.
The weighted theorem assumes precisely nonnegative cell weights with sum one and invokes the proved averaging error, preserving the constant 4d/J independently of the number of cells.

The theorem permits different cell indices, residues and integer test functions for each cell. It does not assume a Gowers conclusion or an inverse correlator. Four new theorems are individually kernel audited.
